english.notes:
(i) Section 9(2) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that where an offence under any of the preceding provisions of this Act was committed in respect of more than one deer the maximum fine which may be imposed under section 9(1) shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each deer.
(ii) Section 12(1) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that if a constable suspects with reasonable cause that any person is committing or has committed an offence under the Act, the constable may without warrant:-
(a) stop and search that person if the constable suspects without reasonable cause that evidence of the commission of the offence is to be found on that person;
(b) search or examine any vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing which that person may then be using if the constable suspects with reasonable cause that evidence of the commission of the offence is to be found on that vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing;
(c) seize and detain for the purposes of proceedings under this Act anything which is evidence of the commission of the offence and any deer, venison, vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing which is liable to be forfeited under section 13.
(iii) Section 12(2) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that for the purposes of-
(a) exercising the powers conferred under subsection (1) above, or
(b) arresting a person, in accordance with section 24 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 (arrest without warrant), for an offence under this Act,
a constable may enter any land other than a dwelling-house.
(iv) Section 12(3) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that a constable may sell any deer or venison seized under this section and the net proceeds of the sale shall be liable to be detained and forfeited in the same manner as the deer or venison sold; but he shall not be subject to any liability on account of his neglect or failure to exercise the powers conferred on him by this subsection.
(v) Section 13(1) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that the court by which a person is convicted of any offence under this Act may order the forfeiture of-
(a) any deer or venison in respect of which the offence was committed or which was found in that person's possession;
(b) any vehicle, animal, weapon or other thing which was used to commit the offence or which was capable of being used to take, kill, or injure deer and was found in his possession.
(vi) Section 13(2) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that where the offence of which the person is convicted is an offence under section 1, the court (without prejudice to its powers under subsection (1) above) may cancel any firearm or shotgun certificate held by him.

other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

In relation to an offence committed after the coming into force of Schedule 26 to the Criminal Justice Act 2003, 51 weeks is to be substituted for three months.

See section 9 re multiple fines where more than one deer is involved.
